verifiedFacts: SUP4 (pdf 6, printed 10-4, LTA/SDRE14/10/SUP4 rev B): low single/double SHS 50x50x2.3 post supports; sign 900 (max) wide x 1000 (max) high; height clearance 'VARIES FROM 500 - 1200'; note 1 lists minimum height clearance 900-1200 mm for sharp deviation barrier signs and 500 mm for Keep Left / Right Pass Either Side signs.

SUP5 (pdf 7, printed 10-5, LTA/SDRE14/10/SUP5 rev B): traffic sign on lamp post or vertical support; left elevation labels 2400 from ground level to bottom edge of sign; sign width 'NOT MORE THAN 900'; holder type 1 variants for panel heights 600 and below, 900 and 1200.

SUP6 (pdf 8, printed 10-6, LTA/SDRE14/10/SUP6 rev C): single post support with SHS 50x50x5.0 hot dipped galvanised, sign 900 (max) wide x 1000 (max) high, 2400 ground to sign bottom, 200x200x10 M.S. plate welded to SHS on 4 expansion bolts, 500x500x1000 C16/20 concrete; double post support 1100-1700 wide, posts 800 apart, 2400 ground to sign bottom, area not exceeding 1.35 m2.

SUP7 (pdf 9, printed 10-7, LTA/SDRE14/10/SUP7, no revision letter): traffic sign holder type 2 for a 600x600 or 600x450 traffic sign, 450 offset (reduce to 100 mm if the sign can clear the top of the vertical support), 2 nos 19 width stainless steel band with buckle around lamp post or vertical support; no installation height stated.

SUP15 (pdf 17, printed 10-15, LTA/SDRE14/10/SUP15 rev A): vertical supports for traffic sign with area not exceeding 1.1 m2 for arterial road (SHS 75x75x3, 600x600x900 C16/20 concrete) and 2.3 m2 for expressway (SHS 100x100x4); both elevations label 2400 from ground to bottom of sign; sign width and height 'VARIES'.
unresolved: No SUP sheet establishes a universal sign mounting height, face normal or lateral offset from the kerb; each 2400 mm label applies only to the assembly drawn on that sheet.
No SUP sheet in the collection covers traffic signal poles, mast arms or signal head brackets.

verifiedFacts: pdf 47 / printed 46 'EXAMPLES': three vertical paired heads (image xrefs 368, 369, 370). Left: circular green + right-arrow green, 'Means GO for straight ahead vehicles and GO for right turn vehicles.' Middle: circular green + right-arrow amber, 'Means GO for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must get ready to STOP.' Right: circular green + right-arrow red, 'Means GO for straight ahead vehicles only. Vehicles turning right must stop behind the stop line.'

pdf 46 / printed 45: GREEN ARROW 'Means GO in the direction indicated. (Turn right)'; AMBER ARROW 'Means READY TO STOP behind the stop-line in the direction indicated.'; RED ARROW 'Means STOP behind the stop-line in the direction indicated. (Do not turn right even when there is no traffic from the opposite direction)'.
pdf 46 / printed 45: GREEN B 'Means GO for all buses only.' with illustration xref 361; the illustration places B to the right of red as seen by the reader.
pdf 11 / printed 10: Give Way 'Slow down. Stop if necessary. Give way to traffic on major road.'; Stop 'Stop before the white line. Give way to traffic from the right and left.'
unresolved: Signal illustrations are small raster images with no housing, pole, bracket or lens dimensions.
No horizontal signal head illustration exists in the handbook pages used here.
Page 2 states reproduction requires publisher permission; reuse remains unreviewed.

verifiedFacts: Vertical circular order: red above amber, green below amber.
Vertical arrow combinations: each arrow light at the same level as the light of the same colour.
Vertical lens: effective diameter at least 200 mm; lowest lens centre 2,290 mm above ground, may be increased to 3,000 mm owing to road gradient; adjacent lens centres not more than 500 mm apart.

Horizontal circular order: red on the right of amber, green on the left of amber (facing approaching traffic); arrow lights below the light of the same colour; lens at least 300 mm; lowest lens centre not less than 5,200 mm.
Additional green light (B) where vertical: at the same level on the left side of or above the red light facing approaching traffic.
An illuminated red arrow prohibits vehicles from proceeding beyond the stop line or broken lines in that direction.
